19.text: As to the rarity of polar bears, the Pacific villages of the Chukchee and Asiatic

20.text: Eskimo are exactly in the same condition as South Greenland, for bears do

21.text: not often stray into these regions.

22.text: The winter hunting on the ice is carried on individually. Still, a man

23.text: who has killed a walrus or a thong-seal takes the whole carcass only in case

24.text: he is all alone on the ice. If others are present, each onlooker has a right

25.text: to take a part. Usually, when a man has killed one of these animals, all those

26.text: who have noticed his good luck start on the run for the place of killing.

27.text: The rule of distribution is as follows: Of a thong-seal, the hunter takes the

28.text: hide, the head, and both shoulder-blades; the first-comer takes the pelvis;

29.text: the second-comer, the right hind-leg; the third-comer, the left hind-leg; the

30.text: fourth one, the brisket; the fifth, the lower ribs, with a corresponding slice

31.text: of blubber all around the body; the other ribs are divided among the other

32.text: claimants. The last-comers receive some piece of fresh meat of the animal.

33.text: All this, of course, occasions much strife and even scuffling. If only one

34.text: comes, the animal is simply cut in two, the hunter taking the upper part, and

35.text: the other man the lower part. Carvings in bone, of the Chukchee and Eskimo,

36.text: often represent such halves of the thong-seal, accurately cut off and loaded

37.text: on a sled, ready to be conveyed to the shore. Of walrus, the hunter takes
